title: Chapter 242: You Are My Next Story
html:
“Even you don’t know who the chairperson is?” Chen Ge thought he could use this question to identify Wu Fei or Patient 10, but he did not expect this answer.

“We all wear identical robes and masks. Even if the person beneath one changes, none of us can tell.” The first man on the left pointed to himself. “I am No. 1. Here, your number matters more than your name. If you don’t want someone to replace you, remain vigilant.”

The warning was directed at No. 12. Her distinctive voice and story had revealed her husband’s surname along with numerous details about her life. Anyone determined enough could identify her.

Since Chen Ge had heard her voice before, he was fairly sure he knew who she was. To be fair, Chen Ge did not expect the famed DJ to be such an individual.

“The society has no other rules beyond the requirement to prepare enough ghost stories.” The man’s voice cooled. “Once each of you has told three, we will do everything possible to grant your wish. After that, you may stay or leave.”

“No. 1 has explained everything you need to know.” The man on the right snapped his fingers. “Dinner will be served shortly. Afterward, you are free to go.”

Dinner?Suspicious though he was, Chen Ge asked nothing. The room fell silent. Half an hour later, footsteps approached in the corridor. The door opened, and the bird-masked man peered inside, fresh scratches visible on his neck. “There was an accident. We need a little more time.”

“No matter. Sunrise is still a long way off.” The first man on the right glanced at the three newcomers. “The first time can be unsettling, but you’ll grow accustomed to it.”

When he finished, No. 10, who liked Chen Ge’s mask, said, “If you’re in a hurry, you can choose to leave first.”

The other black-robed figures remained silent, apparently puzzled by his suggestion.

“In that case, I’ll skip the meal. I need to start searching for new ghost stories.” No. 11 appeared to be the most ordinary person present. He was uncomfortable among these lunatics and would never have attended if he had not been fleeing the police. The figures at the table merely waved him away, their attention fixed on No. 10, whose behavior that night had been unusually curious.

Chen Ge still had much to learn about the Ghost Stories Society, and the bloody strands in his shadow needed only another minute or two to complete their work. Leaving now would be wasteful. With every member gathered in one place, this was the perfect opportunity to capture them all at once.

The chairperson was one of the ten, but even the members did not know which. The simplest solution was therefore to deal with all ten.

“Goodbye. We’ll meet again next Wednesday.” The second newcomer hurried from the room. The bird-masked man remained by the door, watching him like a butcher eyeing a cut of meat.

“Will you two be leaving as well?” No. 10 asked Chen Ge and the woman.

“I’m curious about the food served here.” For the first time, there was emotion in the woman’s tone; she sounded excited. “I’ll stay.”

Running footsteps echoed through the corridor as No. 11 neared the elevator.

“I have an emergency, see you again next Wednesday.” Chen Ge walked out of the room. When he passed the birdman, he smelled a faint hint of blood.

“I’m surprised you walked out alive.” Surprise and confusion colored the bird-masked man’s voice.

“There will be many more surprises in your future.” Chen Ge smiled, making the skin mask especially terrifying.

The birdman did not answer immediately. He waited until Chen Ge had left before grumbling, “For some reason, I am not anticipating them.”

No. 11 stood beside the elevator in his pig mask, jabbing impatiently at the call button while the display changed with agonizing slowness.

“Why is it taking so long?” He felt as though he were suffocating. Compared with those lunatics, the most frightening experience of his life seemed trivial. And the fourth newcomer—how had that man survived so many horrors? “No. I have to leave immediately.”

The elevator climbed but paused on the twenty-third floor. After a long delay, the display finally changed to 24, as though a vast distance separated the two levels. No. 11 rushed inside and pressed the close-door button, unaware that someone had followed him. Just before the silver-gray doors met, a hand stopped them. Chen Ge stepped into the car. “Let’s go together.”

The man silently gulped. He wanted to reject, but he did not have the courage to. “Sure.”

After selecting the first floor, Chen Ge stood beside the doors. Once they had closed completely, he looked back at No. 11. “Will you return next Wednesday?”

“I don’t know. If I find another ghost story, perhaps.” No. 11’s voice was stiff; he wanted no conversation with this man.

“So, you’re worried about that.” Chen Ge laughed. “I know many ghost stories; would you like me to share one with you?”

“You’re willing to share them with me?” Hope rose within No. 11’s heart. If Chen Ge was willing to tell him one ghost story, he only needed to find one more story to get the society to fulfil his wish.

“Of course.” Chen Ge turned as the shadow behind him pulsed. Blood surged outward like a crimson swan unfurling its wings. “After all, you’re the main character!”

Endless black hair erupted from Chen Ge’s shadow, engulfing the elevator.

A woman in a brilliant red dress leaned against his shoulder, her pale, beautiful face contorted by endless suffering.

“Zhang Ya!”

In the enclosed elevator, there was nowhere to run!

Chen Ge lunged forward, tore off No. 11’s mask, and clamped a hand over his mouth. The elevator’s display counted steadily downward, but time itself seemed to slow.

…

When the display reached 1, the doors opened upon a man lying rigid with terror in the corner.

His heart still beat, but fear had erased every other expression. A closer look revealed that his pupils appeared shattered like glass beads, blood leaking from them.

Chen Ge dragged the catatonic Zhu Xiu from the elevator. Zhang Ya floated behind him, playing with a new toy.

The toy looked exactly like Zhu Xiu. From nearby, one could hear a faint scream trapped within it.
